description: Chord generator: builds a chord from a root note and a chord type, and puts it out as four separate 1V/oct pitches and as one polyphonic 1V/oct signal

params.text: Sets the root note of the chord over a range of -4V to 4V, rounded to the nearest semitone, with 0V giving C4
Chooses the chord from major, minor, dominant 7, minor 7, major 7, sus2, sus4, diminished and augmented, one per volt from -4V for major to 4V for augmented
Sets the inversion from 0 for root position to 3; on a three-note chord 3 gives the same voicing as 2
Spreads the chord: 0 leaves it as built, 1 drops the root an octave, 2 drops the root and the fifth, 3 drops the root and raises the third, 4 drops the root and the seventh on a four-note chord

inputs.text: Sets the root note of the chord in place of the Root knob while a cable is patched, read as 1V/oct and rounded to the nearest semitone
Chooses the chord type in place of the Type knob while a cable is patched, one type per volt and clamped to -4V to 4V
Sets the inversion in place of the Inversion knob while a cable is patched, clamped to 0-3V
Sets the voicing in place of the Voicing knob while a cable is patched, clamped to 0-4V

outputs.text: The lowest note of the chord as 1V/oct, after inversion and voicing have been applied
The second note of the chord as 1V/oct, after inversion and voicing have been applied
The third note of the chord as 1V/oct, after inversion and voicing have been applied
The fourth note of the chord as 1V/oct on a seventh chord; on a three-note chord it carries the lowest note raised an octave
The whole chord as a polyphonic 1V/oct signal, three or four channels according to the chord type, lowest note first; the extra octave that output 4 adds to a three-note chord is not included

notes: the display names the chord being built, root and quality together, and it takes no click
